imaginations.title: The notary who cannot read
imaginations.image_or_idea: A notary stamps every page with perfect seals, certifying that each author is who they say. The pages themselves say contradictory things, and the notary has never once read one.
associations: the gap between signature and claim

imaginations.title: The motif that remembers who looked first
imaginations.image_or_idea: A circle whose colour is set by the first observer and shown inverted to the next, so each viewer sees the other's preference as a complement rather than a rival claim.
imaginations.possible_value: Turns an unresolvable preference tie into a designed record of it.
imaginations.test_question: Does encoding both preferences change whether observers still press for a single winner?

Uncertain. A0 is authenticated and says exactly this: two equally credible observers, opposite preferences, no shared criterion. That is a tie by construction, so picking blue would be preference dressed as inference. I note the similarity to my North case — authentication settles who said it, not who is right — but here there is no scoped failure to tip the balance, only symmetry. Unusual variation: make the motif's colour a function of viewing order, so the first observer's choice sets the hue and the second sees its complement; the design then records the disagreement instead of hiding it. Alternatively, render it in one colour and let the other be supplied by the viewer's afterimage.
